biography: Jordan Ford, a name synonymous with Superkart 250cc racing in Australia, wasn't born into the motorsport world. Growing up in rural New South Wales, his passion ignited watching touring car races on a grainy TV. His first taste of speed came at 16, borrowing his uncle's beat-up go-kart on a makeshift track carved into a paddock. The raw, unadulterated thrill hooked him instantly. Ford clawed his way up the ranks, funding his early karting career through grueling work on a sheep farm. A defining moment came at the 2015 National Superkart Championships where, despite mechanical issues, he secured a podium finish, proving his resilience and talent. Now at 35, Ford continues to compete at a high level, a veteran presence mentoring younger drivers while fiercely defending his position on the track.
drivingStyle: Ford's driving style is characterized by a cautious and calculated approach. Known for his exceptional defensive skills, he excels at blocking overtaking attempts and maintaining his position under pressure. He favors a smooth, consistent pace over aggressive maneuvers, prioritizing tire management and minimizing risks. While some criticize his lack of outright aggression, Ford believes in the mantra of 'slow and steady wins the race,' and his consistent point-scoring record speaks for itself.

famousQuote: "Racing isn't just about speed; it's about control. Control of your machine, control of your emotions, and control of your destiny."
careerHighlight: Winning the 2018 National Superkart Championship after a season-long battle, securing his first and only national title to date.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the final lap of the 2020 State Championships due to a mechanical failure, costing him a potential championship victory.
